Area Forecast Discussion
National Weather Service Burlington VT
740 PM EDT Thu Sep 10 2026

.WHAT HAS CHANGED...
As of 242 PM EDT Thursday...

No significant changes to the current forecast.

&&

.KEY MESSAGES...
As of 240 PM EDT Thursday...

1. Breezy conditions today will usher in dry weather for most 
of the weekend.

2. A weak cold front will pass east through the region on 
Sunday and bring breezy conditions, warm temperatures, and 
scattered showers and thunderstorms. 

3. A progressive pattern will support periods of rain showers 
with a trough favored to move through Tuesday night into 
Wednesday.

&&

.DISCUSSION...
As of 240 PM EDT Thursday...

KEY MESSAGE 1: Fast westerly flow is bringing in dry air across
Vermont and northern New York. Temperatures currently range in 
the upper 60s to mid 70s. A well mixed boundary layer has 
resulted in 20-30 mph gusts across the forecast area, and even a
few peak gusts around 35- 40 mph. The expected cold front is 
still off to our north. Radar shows very little activity, and 
strong 700mb layer inversion with low to mid-level drying will 
permit only a rogue shower, if any, as the front crosses 
southeast. Overnight, winds will slacken, but not completely die
off. Additionally, there will be some high clouds initially. 
This will result in slow cooling brought on by the cold 
advection early this evening, and then a sharper drop before 
sunrise when radiational cooling will become more dominant. 
Overnight low temperatures should settle into the lower 40s to 
lower 50s, with perhaps a spot upper 30 for the perennially cold
Adirondack Airport.

Friday will be nice and cool with beautiful weather with mid 
60s to lower 70s. Good radiational cooling will ensue overnight,
but surface high pressure will amble offshore, and a little bit
of southerly return flow will follow. Another night of lower 
40s to lower 50s, and probably a few additional upper 30s in 
colder hollows appears most likely. Saturday will be similar, 
but warming solidly into the 70s with the southerly flow. Then 
Saturday night will be more humid with warmer overnight lows in 
the mid 50s to mid 60s.

KEY MESSAGE 2: Sunday will start warm and humid as a narrow 
tongue of Gulf moisture reaches the forecast area. There's a 
fairly strong upper low moving along Hudson Bay, but its 
attendant surface reflection will be in far northern Quebec 
Province. So the cold front extending south of the surface low 
will be quite elongated over our region. A lee side trough 
enhanced by diurnally driven convection will track along the 
Mid-Atlantic. It will keep the bulk of better instability and 
moisture away from our region, while we only have marginal 
synoptic forcing out of the stretched out frontal boundary. 
Still, good surface heating will push temperatures into the mid 
70s to lower 80s, and this will result in about 750-1250 J/kg of
CAPE. A few showers and thunderstorms seem reasonable, but the 
GFS simulated IR satellite doesn't hint at the potential for 
strong updrafts with a lack of cold cloud tops. Shear does 
appear to be on the high side at 45-50 knots. Given weak 
forcing, only modest instability, and dry air entrainment, that 
shear might just be too much. We'll keep an eye, but the most 
likely case is garden variety scattered showers and 
thunderstorms with breezy conditions ahead of the front.

KEY MESSAGE 3: 500 mb flow in the mid-high latitudes are 
favored to be mainly zonal with Arctic air trapped well north of
the region. Fast- moving troughs will be moving through this 
flow with model trends shifting to a later approach of Tuesday's
wave. As such, chances were lowered Tuesday afternoon and 
shifted later into Tuesday night/Wednesday as the trough moves 
through. Some models keep a stalled surface boundary over the 
region which will have implications to temperatures and 
precipitation chances going forward. Should this come to 
fruition, a wetter period would be possible along/south of this 
boundary. Either way, another wave is projected to move through 
Thursday into the end of the work week with more chances of 
afternoon showers and maybe a rumble of thunder.

&&

.AVIATION /00Z FRIDAY THROUGH TUESDAY/...
Through 00Z Saturday...Surface winds will be light overnight, 
but flow will remain above a very shallow inversion. These 
factors should limit the areal coverage of fog and IFR or lower 
conditions, but SLK/MPV will need to be watched, given recent 
rainfall. Have included 3sm BR at SLK/MPV for now towards early 
morning. Winds remain light out of the west to northwest after 
12Z Friday with VFR conditions prevailing.

Outlook...

Friday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Saturday: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Saturday Night: Mainly VFR, with areas MVFR possible. Slight
chance SHRA.
Sunday: Mainly VFR, with local IFR possible. Chance SHRA, Slight
chance TSRA.
Sunday Night: VFR. Slight chance SHRA.
Monday: Mainly VFR, with local MVFR possible. NO SIG WX.
Monday Night: VFR. NO SIG WX.
Tuesday: VFR. Slight chance SHRA.

&&

.MARINE...
West-northwest to northwest winds across Lake Champlain have
mainly been between 10 to 20 knots. A few gusts at or above 25
knots have occurred. Waves will likely remain around 1 to 3 
feet today. Winds will become weaker this evening around 5 to 
15 knots out of the northwest.

&&

.BTV WATCHES/WARNINGS/ADVISORIES...
VT...None.
NY...None.

&&

$$
